asked.asked:
**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** The tightest tangle in Harbour is between LLM & prompts and Runs & dispatch: the links between the two areas grew from 32 one way and 50 the other to 38 and 55 over batch 1 (Seams run 12). On this side:

* the list of routes that code settles without asking a model is copied about nine times, and `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md` and `public/llms.txt` already describe it wrongly (Drift, row 154);
* the blind read's name and heading are retyped outside the file that defines them (Drift, row 151);
* batch 1 added rules to the prompts as text (the frozen prompt total rose about 21,000 bytes, to 378,915). John on that limit: "That limit is to push against lists if rules. Worth knowing, but not hard and fast.";
* LIN-4350 asks to fold the rules together into plainer, more general instructions.

The safety pass (A5, LIN-4400) found two themes here: merge and read-only limits that exist only in prompt text (LIN-1242, LIN-1273, LIN-3417), and tokens inside prompt text (LIN-1372, LIN-1395, LIN-1408). Both are part of A12 (LIN-4416). The area's note holds 26 Waiting entries.

**What we want.**

* Each rule has one home; the copies are gone, and the docs say what the code does.
* A limit that matters is held in code, not only in a prompt's words.
* Fewer rules are restated as lists in prompt text.
* The area's Waiting entries are settled, or each says why it can't be yet.
* Each piece finishes one move and names what it retired; piece sizes vary, leaning larger.
* The Runs & dispatch side of the seam is A13's.

**Done when**

* the cases above are settled, or John has ruled they can wait;
* the safety tickets named above are closed in code for that reason, or John has ruled they can wait;
* the area's Waiting entries are settled or say why not;
* the area reads better in a blind read after this work than before it, by more than an untouched area read at the same times.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

index.line: `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` and the budget test change in almost every merge: rebase, then re-measure. Its fixture passes no context (the empty-context branch), so dropping one can raise a ceiling while real renders shrink (LIN-4393).

`lib/prompt-template-defs.js` cannot import what imports `lib/prompt-templates.js` (a cycle): shared words live in an import-free leaf, as `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` (LIN-4376) and `lib/prompts/autopilot-precedence.js` (never restate a rank; LIN-4382).

The kit cannot be used fully unchanged: `docs/plans/survey/area-read.md` names Runs as the work area, posts to LIN-4447 under `@ 4b5001ddf` headings and writes the verdict as D = Δ(Runs) − Δ(control). The salt and N=14 carry over; the area, base, target ticket and verdict wording do not. Editing the kit breaks its blob pin (kit `cbec2d848`, reader prompt `ef1c2ca91`, both unchanged at `e8e92d50a`) for LIN-4462's after-read, so leave the file alone and record them in each report's header: area, base `e8e92d50a` (origin/main, the #2426/LIN-4456 merge, after `5dcf5bcda`), target LIN-4448, verdict mapping, the byte-imbalance limit, the full contamination list, `areas.json` blob `1dc2ba701` (no change to either sample), the LLM note blob `b6b4c726d` (25 Waiting entries). Order: fix the base at `e8e92d50a` even if main moves, provided none of pieces 1–6 has landed; write the header before running any reader; then four fresh passes.

The pairing is not balanced the way the kit claims. The kit chose N=14 for a 3.4% byte gap (Runs vs control); at `e8e92d50a` the samples are 380,459 B for llm-and-prompts (14 of 91 files) and 206,545 B for front-end-pages (14 of 92), 1.84×. `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` (120,531 B) and `lib/openrouter.js` (103,188 B) are 59% of the LLM sample, so K3/K4 will mostly score those two files; each pass takes about 395 KB (sample plus the 14,838 B note), nearly twice the bundle size that forced the kit's file-path delivery, and the noise guard (≥1.0 apart) is more likely to trip. N is frozen: record the gap as a known limit in both reports, don't fix it. The kit's Known limits 1–2 flip here: all three planned files (`openrouter`, `prompt-template-defs`, `recommendation-live-wait`) are sampled (ranks 1, 5, 8), so the read is sensitive to the work but mostly measures two files. Do not copy kit limits 1–2; they would state the opposite of what is true.

The control has more contamination than the ticket says. Three of its 14 sample files changed since `4b5001ddf`: `lib/render-proxy.js` (812d9adbb, #2424, as noted), and `lib/render-swipe.js` and `lib/render-task-page.js` from #2423 (LIN-4446), which the ticket does not mention; `render-task-page.js` is also one of LIN-4453's four tracked files. The control's note changed too: `front-end-pages.md` went from 6,404 B to 5,825 B (blob `ae9c007e1`), Waiting entries 14 to 12. All of it falls inside this baseline (base `e8e92d50a`), so the pair holds; record all of it in both reports. This control read's M scores will not match LIN-4453's baseline. Because the salt is unchanged, the control paths match LIN-4453's, so this read is a free midpoint for LIN-4453: note that, don't claim it.

Open PRs at `e8e92d50a`: #2426 (LIN-4456) has merged and is the base. #2427 (LIN-4455) and the eleven other open PRs touch neither sample (28 files). Record that in both reports. Write PRs as `#2427`, never full URLs: a report posted as a comment that names a full PR URL joins the ticket's landing, because `landingPrUrls` skips only blind reads and survey reports (Runs Waiting entry, LIN-4453 leftover).

Smaller traps: (1) "frozen prompt" in the done-when means the kit's reader prompt, not the parent's 378,915 B prompt budget. (2) The reader prompt's K2 examples are about Runs (close-out, PRs per task, dispatch model); they are frozen, so note it in both reports; Δ is still sound, but do not compare absolute scores across areas. (3) Commit the reports as `docs/plans/survey/area-read-reports/{llm-and-prompts,front-end-pages}-e8e92d50a.md`, as in #2422. (4) If you also post them as comments, use the `## Area read:` heading, not `## Blind read` (422).

Where it lands: in `docs/plans/survey/` (the kit, the method-as-run addendum, `area-read-reports/`). The kit is frozen but written as a one-off: its table, its headings (`@ 4b5001ddf`, "comment on LIN-4447"), its verdict (Δ Runs − Δ control) and its Known limits all name Runs; only the snippet and the prompt take parameters. This is its second use. Do not copy `area-read-method-as-run.md` and swap Runs for LLM: that leaves a second copy of the method beside a kit whose words do not fit this read. Instead write one short addendum that cites the kit by blob (`cbec2d848`, prompt `ef1c2ca91`) and lists only what differs: base, area, byte gap, flipped limits, the six-file import table and the control's three moved files. Full recorded fields go in each report, as in #2422.
